question.text:
\[ \underbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 7 & 0 \\ -12 & 32 & 1 \\ -3 & -13 & -10 \end{bmatrix} }_{\large A} = \underbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -5 & 1 \end{bmatrix} }_{\large L} \cdot \underbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 7 & 0 \\ \fbox{$\phantom{\,N\,}$} & \fbox{$\phantom{\,N\,}$} & \fbox{$\phantom{\,N\,}$} \\ 0 & 0 & -5 \end{bmatrix} }_{\large U}. \]

Consider the LU factorization of the matrix $A$ above. From left to right, what are the missing elements from the second row of the matrix $U?$
question.explanation:
The matrix $U$ in the LU decomposition is obtained from the original matrix $A$ by row-reducing using Gaussian elementation. In particular, to make $0$ at the position $a_{21}$ of the matrix $A,$ we proceed as follows:

\[ \begin{align*} A &= \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 7 & 0 \\ -12 & 32 & 1 \\ -3 & -13 & -10 \end{bmatrix} & R_2 & := R_{2} + (-4)R_{1} \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 7 & 0 \\ \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{0} & \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{4} & \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{1} \\ -3 & -13 & -10 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*} \]

Therefore, from left to right, the elements from the second row of $U$ are $0,4,$ and $1.$

Consider the LU factorization of the matrix $A$ above. What is the value of the entry $l_{21}$ in the matrix $L?$
question.explanation:
We want to make $0$ at the position $a_{{\color{blue}2}{\color{red}1}}$ using Gaussian elimination. To do this, we take the ${\color{blue}2}$nd row of $A,$ and we add the ${\color{red}1}$st row of $A$ multiplied by ${\color{purple}}{:}$

\[ \begin{align*} A &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -6 & 6 \\ \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{-4} & 6 & 0 \\ -10 & 6 & 4 \end{bmatrix} & R_2 & := R_{\color{blue}2} + \left( {\color{purple}2} \right) R_{\color{red}1} \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -6 & 6 \\ \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{0} & -6 & 12 \\ -10 & 6 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*} \]

The entry $l_{{\color{blue}2}{\color{red}1}}$ of the matrix $L$ is the factor next to $R_1,$ taken with the opposite sign:

\[ l_{21}=-({\color{purple}2})=-2. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the LU Factorization of a 3x3 Matrix

question.text:
\[ D= \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 2 & 3\\ -4 & 6 & 7 \\ 8 & -8 & -11 \end{bmatrix} \]

If $D=LU$ is the LU decomposition of the matrix $D$ given above, what is the value of $l_{31} \cdot u_{22}?$
question.explanation:
Let's apply our standard LU factorization algorithm.

We reduce the matrix $D$ to row echelon form to obtain the matrix $U,$ as usual. However, instead of writing zeros below the main diagonal, we will instead write down the entries of the matrix $L.$

\[ \begin{align*} D &= \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 2 & 3 \\ -4 & 6 & 7 \\ 8 & -8 & -11 \end{bmatrix} & R_2 & := R_2 + ({\color{blue}-2}) R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 2 & 3 \\ \bbox[FloralWhite, 2pt, border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid black]{\color{blue}2} & 2 & 1 \\ 8 & -8 & -11 \end{bmatrix} & R_3 & := R_3 + {\color{red}4} R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 2 & 3 \\ \bbox[FloralWhite, 2pt, border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid black]{2} & 2 & 1 \\ \bbox[FloralWhite, 2pt, border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid black]{\color{red}-4} & \bbox[FloralWhite, 2pt, border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid black]{0} & 1 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*} \]

Therefore, we obtain
\[ L= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad U= \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

Finally, since $l_{31}=-4$ and $u_{22}=2,$ we get

\[ l_{31} \cdot u_{22} = (-4) \cdot 2 =-8. \]

question.text:
\[ A= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 & -4 \\ 4 & 14 & -16 \\ 3 & 13 & -11 \end{bmatrix} \]

If $A=LU$ is the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ given above, what is the value of $l_{32} \cdot u_{23}?$
question.explanation:
Let's apply our standard LU factorization algorithm.

We reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form to obtain the matrix $U,$ as usual. However, instead of writing zeros below the main diagonal, we will instead write down the entries of the matrix $L.$

\[ \begin{align*} A &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 & -4 \\ 4 & 14 & -16 \\ 3 & 13 & -11 \end{bmatrix} & R_2 & := R_2 + \left( {\color{blue}-4} \right) R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 & -4 \\ \bbox[FloralWhite, 2pt, border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid black]{\color{blue}\:\:4\:\:} & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & 13 & -11 \end{bmatrix} & R_3 & := R_3 + ({\color{red}-3}) R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 & -4 \\ \bbox[FloralWhite, 2pt, border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid black]{\:\:4\:\:} & 2 & 0 \\ \bbox[FloralWhite, 2pt, border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid black]{\color{red}3} & 4 & 1 \end{bmatrix} & R_3 & := R_3 + ({\color{purple}-2})R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 & -4 \\ \bbox[FloralWhite, 2pt, border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid black]{\:\:4\:\:} & 2 & 0 \\ \bbox[FloralWhite, 2pt, border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid black]{3} & \bbox[FloralWhite, 2pt, border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid black]{\color{purple}\:2\:} & 1 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*} \]

Therefore, we obtain
\[ L= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad U= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

question.text:
\[ C= \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 9 & -3 \\ 4 & 12 & 0 \\ 4 & 6 & -3 \end{bmatrix} \]

If $C=LU$ is the LU decomposition of the matrix $C$ given above, what is the value of $l_{21} \cdot u_{23}?$
question.explanation:
Let's apply our standard LU factorization algorithm.

We reduce the matrix $C$ to row echelon form to obtain the matrix $U,$ as usual. However, instead of writing zeros below the main diagonal, we will instead write down the entries of the matrix $L.$

\[ \begin{align*} A &= \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 9 & -3 \\ 4 & 12 & 0 \\ 4 & 6 & -3 \end{bmatrix} & R_2 & := R_2 + \left( {\color{blue}-1} \right) R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 9 & -3 \\ \bbox[FloralWhite, 2pt, border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid black]{\color{blue}\:\:1\:\:} & 3 & 3 \\ 4 & 6 & -3 \end{bmatrix} & R_3 & := R_3 + \left( {\color{red}-1} \right) R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 9 & -3 \\ \bbox[FloralWhite, 2pt, border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid black]{\:\:1\:\:} & 3 & 3 \\ \bbox[FloralWhite, 2pt, border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid black]{\color{red}\:\:1\:\:} & -3 & 0 \end{bmatrix} & R_3 & := R_3 + {\color{purple}1} R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 9 & -3 \\ \bbox[FloralWhite, 2pt, border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid black]{\:\:1\:\:} & 3 & 3 \\ \bbox[FloralWhite, 2pt, border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid black]{\:\:1\:\:} & \bbox[FloralWhite, 2pt, border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid black]{\color{purple}-1} & 3 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*} \]

Finally, since $l_{21}=1$ and $u_{23}=3,$ we get

\[ l_{21} \cdot u_{23} = 1 \cdot 3 =3. \]
